Violation ID: 932770
Permit API: 125-28879
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Jefferson Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 10/06/2021
Comments: On October 6, 2021, The Department received a reportable release from Range Resources. According to the report, approximately more than 42 gallons of flow back water was spilled at the MCC West Well Site in Jefferson Township, Washington County. I contacted Operator representative Dennis Furmanek, Mr. Furmanek indicated that the release was identified during an inspection at approximately 11:50am and was reported to PADEP at 13:26. Mr. Furmanek indicated that release occurred when a cam lock connection leaked. The release occurred on secondary containment, however upon further investigation the fluid was released to the ground and the channel adjacent to the well pad. Mr. Furmanek indicated that the Operator intends to utilize Act 2 for cleanup. I informed Mr. Furmanek that I would conduct an onsite follow up inspection on 10/7/2021. The Operator in compliance with the current Department spill policy, however violations area being issued due to amount of fluid lost.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/05/2025 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Township, Tioga county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/05/2025
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8232013
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/05/2025
Comments: Site inspection conducted to review drill cuttings processing activity and secondary containment conditions at the Taft 851 well pad. Meeting on site today with Seneca Company Man Carlos Martinez. Weather conditions are foggy with light rain and 60F.According to Mr. Martinez, the Patterson 805 rig is drilling the 12 1/4 intermediate section on the 206HU well (API # 117- 22267). This is the first of eight total to be drilled. The intermediate casing is expected to be cemented on Wednesday evening at a depth of 3,329'. The 206HU will be drilled top to total depth with the rig batch drilling the surface and intermediate sections for the remaining seven wells. There are five wells in production and currently flowing to sales at this pad. Fluid control in the rig backyard is being handled by Paragon Integrated Services. The rig is drilling the intermediate string on water based mud (WBM) with polymer flocculants and calcium nitrate in use to assist removal of solids from the drilling fluid. Drill cuttings are removed from the system using two sets of shakers and two centrifuges. Fluid removed from the centrifuges is returned to a catch tank and pumped back to the mud tanks for recirculation downhole (photos 3-5). Solids control in the backyard is being conducted by White's Energy Services. Drill cuttings and excess liquid are solidified using wood crumble material and are stored in steel bins awaiting haulage to the landfill. Seneca submitted a Request for Approval of Alternate Waste Management Practices (OG-71) Form A application for the Taft Pad on 4/25/25. The Department approved the request on 5/1/25. The request for the approval of Alternative Waste Management Practices is for drill cuttings processing and solids removal from drilling mud. See photos and comments in the on-site processing findings section of this inspection report below, and refer to the Taft OG-71 Form A application, eFACTS Authorization ID#1525611.Site inspection followed several days of heavy precipitation. A vacuum truck is pumping precipitation water out of secondary containment structures for the frac tank battery at the west side of the pad. The Department observed yellow floc water tanks labeled as cement water near the north side of the rig. The Department recommends that floc water tanks and freshwater tanks near the barite silos be labeled for contents. During this inspection, fluid with elevated conductivity (4.74 mS/cm) is observed in the ditch line between the pad rock and the berm along the north side of the well pad (photo 13). This water was traced and found to be entering Sediment Basin 1 along the rock lined channel sloping down from the pad surface. Additionally, water was observed draining from the sed basin, entering the level spreader, and exiting to a brushy wooded area north of the LOD with a conductivity reading of 2.16 mS/cm. The Department recommends containing and collecting water which exceeds the Department 78a.60b(3) discharge limitation of 1,000 uS/cm or 1 mS/cm. Violations remain outstanding against permit #117-22231 for pollutional water found on site and documented in Inspection Reports #3736567 and #3724668.

Valve closed on main tubular feeding separator and closed valves to and from separator (photo #5). A 31-day production chart is present, with no markings dated 12/1/22 (photo #6). No production is being recorded. Well posting signage affixed to steel tank with all information about well and current Operator present, except the Operator contact address information (photo #7). The Department is requesting Operator add contact address information to the permanent well posting signage affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, and 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 0 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 0 Mcf recorded over 365 days. The 2021 annual production report submitted indicates that this well was not in production during the 2021 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having 0 or blank production values under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the 2021, 2020, and 2019 production reports. The last reported production value was in 2018 of 332 Mcf recorded over 214 days. This well is shut in with no recorded production at the surface/ground production facility and continues to be temporarily not producing.

Violation ID: 995317
Permit API: 015-23792
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Drilling/Alteration
Inspection Date: 5/16/2023
Comments: On 5/16/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Mowry 2 well site. It was 64 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. I did not witness any personnel at the site when I started the inspection. Frac operations have ceased and most of the fracking equipment has been removed from the site. There are still ten 400-barrel tanks, one freshwater AST and one gas buster frac tank on site. Site secondary containment used during the fracking operations still remains in place. The two existing wells and the two newly drilled and fracked wells have not been staged for production yet. I did not witness any bubbling coming from the well cellars. I did field test water within each of the secondary containments with the results showing elevated conductance in each containment with readings as high as 15.32 mS conductance. I did get a reading with a soil probe on the unprotected pad surface south of the brine unloading station secondary containment that field tested at 2.009 mS conductance. I did witness three unmarked 55-gallon drums and some garbage in the secondary containments on the northeast corner of the pad. I did witness secondary containment matting with visible evidence of an oily substance stacked on the unprotected pad surface along the east side of location. There was a 10" x 6" spot underneath the matting that was dark stained.Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. There are areas along the north and east fill slopes that do not meet the 70% uniform perennial vegetative requirement. PCSM is addressed on site by two retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3455915 for elevated conductance fluid detected on the unprotected pad surface during drilling operations.The DEP recommends the following:1. Ensure that good housekeeping practices are conducted when the secondary containments are removed from the site.2. Identify the contents of the three 55-gallon drums and remove the drums and garbage from the site.3. Assess the area of the pad under and south of the brine unloading station secondary containment for possible contamination and remove/report as necessary.4. Remove the stack of matting with oily residue from the site and remove the contaminated soil that is found underneath the stack. I left the site at 1145 hours.

Comments: On 4/07/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection at the Clara Jacques 3 well site in Wharton Township, Fayette County. This inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well, which was submitted by the operator on 3/25/2026. A CO and A was entered into between the Department and Diversified on 3/07/2019. According to the CO and A, Diversified is to restore the Well Site after in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216; after completion of plugging operations.The following was observed during the inspection:The access road is graveled leading to the well plugging site. However, where the access road meets the well plugging site, no stone was observed. The lack of stone in this location appears to be resulting in heavy tire rutting (photos 10-12). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) appears to be installed around the perimeter of the well plugging site in accordance with the on-site E and S plan. Well plugging operations appear to be ongoing at the time of inspection. No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on site during this inspection. The API number and operator's information are posted on the disconnected brine tank at the time of inspection. While on site, Department reviewed the site E and S plan and found that a Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is shown in the location where the heavy tire rutting was observed (photo 21).Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued for failure to follow the E and S plan on site.

Comments: On August 26, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection on the Janoscrat 1 well in Derry Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection CEI inspection in response to violations issued under inspection 3400883 where violations were issued due to a possible brine discharge that was discovered on July 29, 2022. The following was observed:The brine tank from where the possible discharge occurred in inspection 3400883 has since been removed, and the area has been mulched and seeded (see photos 1 and 2). The hissing sound and gas odor previously noted on the well head in inspections 3400883 and 3399998 is no longer present (see photo 4). Newly updated operator's information has also been added (see photo 3). Soil conductivity readings were taken on both sides of what once appeared to be the brine puddle. The one taken on the side closest to the well at the former location of the brine tank read, .49 Micro Siemens (see photo 6). The one taken on the side farthest away from the well read .44 Micro Siemens (see photo 7). An additional reading was taken on the side closest to the well at the former brine tank location, but approximately 6 inches of soil was dug before the reading was taken. It read .38 Micro Siemens. A background reading was taken 50 feet west of the well which read .24 Micro Siemens (see photo 9). Overall, the conductivity of the soil at the site of the possible brine release appears to now be comparable to the surrounding soil.Based on observations from today's inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been removed as of August 26, 2022. However, outstanding violations issued during inspection record 3400883 shall remain open since no NOV response or any of the information requested has been received from the operator.

Violation Code: 78A73(C)____ - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION – Operator failed to cease stimulating the well when visual monitoring indicated a well communication incident had taken place, when treatment pressure or volume changes indicative of abnormal fracture propagation were observed or when otherwise made aware of a confirmed communication incident
Violation ID: 960310
Permit API: 059-28088
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Springhill Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/23/2022
Comments: The Department conducted an inspection of the EQT Lumber 13H well on 6/23/2022. Hydraulic fracturing crews are on site. EQT stopped stimulation activities on the Lumber 13H after a landowner notified the operator of a communication incident on 6/19/2022. The Department became aware of the communication incident on 6/20/2022 and Department personnel responded to the incident. Based on the Departments investigation, the Department has determined the following. EQT was notified by the landowner on 6/19/2022 of the communication incident. EQT investigated and determined hydraulic fracturing operations at the Lumber well site communicated to an offset well. EQT personnel observed fluid and gas expressing from the offset well. EQT stopped stimulation activities on the Lumber 13H and the fluid and gas observations at the offset well subsided. Stimulation operations began on the Lumber 13H well on 5/29/2022. The offset well is approximately 6500 feet from the EQT Lumber 13H well. Prior to stopping stimulation activities, EQT completed 99 of 141 planned stages on the Lumber 13H well. Stage 100 is perforated but not completed on the Lumber 13H well. The offset well is approximately 3200 feet from stages 99 and 100 of the Lumber 13H well. Stages 99 and 100 are approximately 7820 TVD from ground level. Pursuant to 25 Pa. Code Section 78a.73, unconventional operators who are stimulating wells by way of hydraulic fracturing are required to notify the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) upon confirmation of a hydraulic fracturing communication incident. EQT did not notify the Department of the communication incident. A violation of 78a.73(c). Following notification, Technical Guidance Document (TGD) 800-0810-001, Guidelines for Implementing Area of Review (AOR) Regulatory Requirement for Unconventional Wells, describes the incident report that should be electronically filed within 3 days of the incident. The Department has not received the Area of Review Fracturing Communication Incident Report. The Department requests EQT to submit the incident report. At the time of the communication event, EQT was hydraulically fracturing multiple wells (1H, 5H, 13H, 15H) simultaneously. EQT continued hydraulic fracturing operations on an adjacent well (Lumber 11H) after the communication incident was confirmed. A violation of 78a.73(c). The Department requested EQT cease all hydraulic fracturing operations on June 21, 2022. EQT stopped hydraulic fracturing operations at the Lumber well site on 6/22/2022 at approximately 0900. Comments: Incident inspection of Repsol's "DCNR 587 017" Marcellus well site.Megan DePue (Repsol, Remediation and Reclamation) called the DEP today to report that Pete Lorson (Repsol, Facilities) discovered an estimated 10 gallons of drilling mud leaked thru liner containment onto the gravel pad surface. She emailed that the mud used on these wells was water based for the top portion, and diesel based for the deeper section. I spoke with Lorson on site who explained the following: Repsol finished drilling the 7 new Marcellus wells at this site about 2 weeks ago. Today they removed some of the matting to check for subsidence where pipes attached to the Marcellus wells are buried, and discovered some drilling mud leaked thru breaches in the liner.When I arrived on site at about 1415 hrs they were mostly done with the excavation of the impacted pad material. They filled one dumpster with the pad material, and were waiting on another dumpster to dispose of the remaining material that was excavated into a pile. I used a MiniRae 3000 Photo Ionization Detector with a 10.6 eV lamp to screen the excavated area. It returned a 0.0 ppm reading, indicating absence of volatile substances in the material. I also screened the top of a Marcellus well cellar, which returned a 0.4 ppm reading. I used a Hanna Groline soil probe and got 0.23-0.39 mS/cm electrical conductivity readings in the excavated area.Air temp 78FJLP

Comments: On May 15, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up Inspection of the RWS Development 001 Well in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release.At the time of this inspection, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. All other production equipment appeared removed.It appeared excavation had been conducted in the area where the production equipment was removed, as well as the ditch from behind the production equipment area to where the boom was installed. Conductivity readings were taken in the ditch in several locations with readings of 0.39mS, 0.37mS, 0.49mS, and 0.26mS.The Department recommends the operator promptly install/implement temporary erosion and sediment controls. The Department also recommends the operator temporarily stabilize any disturbed areas with in 4 days following cessation of earth disturbance activities.Based on today's inspection, violation remain outstanding as a notice of intent to conduct Act 2 remediation has not yet been received by the Department.

Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/17/2026
Violation Code: 78.64(d)2 - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator drained tank containment facilities without responsible supervision and failed to follow proper drainage procedure.
Violation ID: 8278640
Permit API: 123-47075
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Cherry Grove Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/17/2026
Comments: This inspection is being conducted in response to the observation of production fluid exiting the secondary containment of the Lot 740 tank battery. Conventional well Lot 740 15 (API # 123-47075) is nearest the tank battery. The conventional well appears to be plumbed for production. An old sign displaying the API number, well name, and the wrong operator contact information is posted on a tree near the location. The sign should be updated with the current operator's name and contact information. The tank battery at the site has 2 steel tanks and a separator situated within an earthen secondary containment. The secondary containment was approximately 60ft x 20ft. Evidence of staining, dead vegetation, numerous deer tracks, and conductivity readings over range (greater than 20,000 mS/cm maximum that field meter can measure) were present in standing water throughout the entire secondary containment. This would indicate a large volume of production fluid filled the entire containment at one time (see photo 1). At the time of the inspection, the ground within the secondary containment was saturated with production fluid with some ponding throughout. A small amount of crude oil was also identified within the escaped production fluid. A containment drain inlet was located at a low point in the front left corner within the containment. A conductivity reading of 17.17 mS/cm was measured at the drain inlet (see photo 2). The ponding production fluid was flowing into the drain's inlet, exiting the containment through the drain outlet located at the exterior front left corner of the secondary containment (see photo 3). The containment drain was open and unattended at the time of this inspection. Sample 001 was collected at 13:10 at the containment drain outlet for further testing. A conductivity reading was also taken at this location measuring over range (see photo 4). The production fluid flowed from the containment drain into the road ditch traveling south approximately 50 feet (see photo 5). The escaped production fluid also flowed north in the road ditch approximately 10 feet before entering a road culvert where it continued westward into the woods for approximately 150 feet (see photo 6). The vegetation in the path of flow was dead, the ground was muddy and imprinted with deer tracks, and the conductivity readings measured high throughout the entire length of travel. The conductivity was measured near the apparent end of impact with a reading of 8.51 mS/cm in a puddle.The containment drain is required to be closed when unattended and the regulations state that any discharge is to only consist of precipitation that accumulates inside the containment, not production fluids. On June 18, 2026 a phone call was made to the operator, John McCool, in which he stated his intentions to work towards achieving compliance. He explained that the fluids currently stored in the tanks will be pumped empty and examined for leaks. If any leaks are identified, the tanks will be repaired or replaced. An excavator will be used to remove the contaminated soil within the secondary containment and beyond the containment drain exit following the path of travel through the woods. Upon disposing of the contaminated soils at an approved facility, a copy of the disposal slip from the landfill is expected to be provided to the Department. Confirmatory sampling will be required to confirm the impacts from the release have been sufficiently remediated. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites and Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. Follow up inspections will be performed routinely until the cleanup is deemed complete.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/30/2025 to K PETROLEUM INC in Somerset Township, Washington county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8254341
Permit API: 125-22515
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/30/2025
Comments: On October 30th, 2025, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of K Petroleum Inc's Mclvaine well site located in Somerset Township, Washington County following a voicemail and phone conversation where Operator Robert Inghram notified the Department of a 7-10 gallon release of crude oil from the production tank on to the ground within the tanks earthen dike. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the wellhead and a well posting fixed to the meter box on site, both of which had all required information posted on it. No active surface fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the wellhead, meter box, separator or fenced in production equipment on site.Upon inspection of the production tank, the Department observed a black tank to be within an earthen dike. The tank was observed to have orange/tan smudges and dried drip marks going down the side of it. What the Department believes may be peatsorb was observed on the ground at the base of the tank on top of puddles of fluid. This fluid had a possibly petroleum based odor and was observed to have an orange/tan film on top of it in some areas.The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the dike and collected soil conductivity readings of 0.826 mS and 0.904 mS in the release area, and 0.582 mS in berm of the dike. The Department also collected soil conductivity readings of 0.1705 mS and 0.1746 mS outside of where the peatsorb was observed. All of these readings were then compared to a background soil conductvitiy reading of 0.242 mS. The readings collected outside of the peatsorb are comparable to the background reading, subjugating that the release may be contained to the areas where peatsorb is observed. The readings within the fluid and in the side of the berm are elevated when compared to the background reading subjugating that the release has yet to be fully cleaned up.The Department recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with the Department's policy for small spills. The Operator is also requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.While on site, the Department spoke with Operator Robert Inghram and informed him of the Department's findings and of the aforementioned recommendations and requests. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for a 7-10 gallon release on to the ground from the production tank.
